title: Prime-power matrix exponents give prime-power group order
statement: Let $p$ be a prime natural number, $R$ a commutative ring, $d\geq0$, and $G$ a finite subgroup of the invertible $d\times d$ matrices over $R$ [def-weil-matrix]. Here multiplication is matrix multiplication, identity is $I_d$, and invertible means possessing a two-sided matrix inverse. Suppose that for every $g\in G$ there is an integer $a\geq0$ such that $g^{p^a}=I_d$. Then there is an integer $b\geq0$ such that $|G|=p^b$.
